subject: Climate & Environment
title: Landfill Methane Emissions
description: A quick win: understand Landfill Methane Emissions.

hook.text: Landfills are the third-largest source of methane emissions in the United States.

buildup.text: Organic waste trapped under layers of garbage decomposes without oxygen, producing methane.

discovery.text: Methane is 80 times more potent than CO₂ as a greenhouse gas over 20 years.

twist.text: Capturing landfill methane can generate electricity — but most landfills don't bother.

climax.text: The simplest fix is composting organic waste before it reaches the landfill.

punchline.text: Rotting food in a landfill heats the planet. In compost, it feeds it.

quiz.question: Why do landfills produce methane?
options: Organic waste decomposes without oxygen underground
Chemical reactions between metal and water

details.summary: Landfills produce roughly 11 percent of global methane emissions as organic waste decomposes without oxygen. Methane is over 80 times more potent than CO2 as a greenhouse gas over 20 years. Capturing landfill gas for energy reduces emissions while producing electricity or heat.
details.whyItMatters: Cutting landfill methane is one of the fastest ways to slow near-term warming. Diverting organic waste from landfills and capturing gas from existing sites offer immediate climate benefits.
takeaways: Landfills produce about 11 percent of global methane emissions
Methane is over 80 times more potent than CO2 over 20 years
Gas capture converts methane into usable energy

faq.question: How is landfill gas captured?
faq.answer: Vertical wells and horizontal collectors are drilled into the waste mass to extract gas under vacuum. The collected methane is either burned in engines to generate electricity, processed to pipeline-quality natural gas, or flared to convert it to the less potent CO2.

faq.question: Would composting eliminate landfill methane?
faq.answer: Diverting all organic waste to composting or anaerobic digestion would dramatically reduce landfill methane because organics are the primary source. Studies suggest this could cut landfill emissions by 50 to 70 percent in countries with high food waste.
